Along with P-selectin, this protein is found in Weibel-Palade bodies, and desmopressin can increase expression of this protein. Cryoprecipitate notably contains this protein, which contains an RGD domain for binding to integrin IIb-3. Bernard-Soulier syndrome results when the glycoprotein receptor for this protein is mutated, and this protein clings to Factor VIII in the blood until thrombin separates them. The disease named for this protein is the most common coagulation disorder in the world. Name this glycoprotein whose mutation causes a hemophilia-like syndrome, named for a Finnish guy.

Its title figure is a tamer of horses and a killer of tigers. He also joins the "the cult to Hercules with the cult to Mammon" and is an "Energy Professor as the crazies of today put it." The title figure, who is four hundred parts Nimrod, is responsible for leading an entity that lacks one thing: God! Name this poem about an American President's conquests, a work of Ruben Dario.

originalQuestion: Derrida opaquely claims that the title concept of this work is "irreducibly heterogeneous" and that it is "null" because it prevents language from "circling back to its meaning." The third chapter of this work analyzes the Roman legal concept of nexum to conclude that the Greco-Roman culture was the only ancient culture that did not have an "outmoded morality." It analyzes the Maori's distinction between tonga and oloa, which are objects distinguished on their permanence. This work claims that the title construct is useful in allowing people to distribute the "superabundance of happiness" and rid evil by sacrificing to good gods at the same time. It also proposes several examples of total presentation in less multivalent cultures. Subtitled "the form and reason of exchange in primitive society" it expands upon Malinowski's study of the Kula Ring. For 10 points, name this work of Marcel Mauss.
originalAnswer: The Gift or Essai Sur Le Don
